output:
To: t-4471
Replying to: p01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: PSA: think twice about that "free" eviction clinic

We hear the concern in this thread, and we understand why. Getting a letter from a landlord law firm soon after asking for help is frightening. We are sorry for the worry this has caused. We are not writing to dispute anyone's experience; we want to answer the questions raised here and make sure everyone knows Saturday's clinic is still happening.

Cascade Legal Rights Project's policy prohibits landlords and their attorneys from receiving attendee information. It also prohibits sharing, selling, or disclosing attendee information for any purpose. These rules apply to every clinic we hold. Sign-in records are retained internally in locked storage. We do not discuss any individual's situation publicly, even to defend ourselves, so we will not address specific cases here.

Some tenant mailings come from magistrate-court eviction filings, which are public records. We know some firms use those filings to send solicitations. That is a likely explanation for letters people have received. That does not make the letters any less upsetting, but it is important context.

The Nov. 14 clinic is still on. The library meeting room is closed that day for HVAC repairs, so the clinic will be at Mt Zion Fellowship Hall, same hours, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Use the side entrance by the parking lot; it is accessible. Walk-ins are welcome. Volunteer attorneys and staff can review eviction notices and court papers and explain your options. You can bring any notices or court papers you have. No appointment needed.

Questions can go to clinic@cascaderights.example or the office at 404-555-0187. If you are worried or have questions, please come. You are still welcome.

Cascade Legal Rights Project
